issues.title: CT5-V eLSD 'Service Rear Axle' Message with DTC C1135 SYM92 / Differential Control Module Startup Delay
issues.description: On CT5-V models equipped with the Electronic Limited-Slip Rear Differential (eLSD), owners report a 'Service Rear Axle' message in the Driver Information Center, often accompanied by reduced eLSD function or temporary loss of torque vectoring. The Differential Control Module (DCM) can experience a startup delay or communication fault that sets DTC C1135 with symptom byte 92, sometimes shortly after a cold start. GM issued a service update (N202312960) and multiple Preliminary Information bulletins (PIP5763, PIP5763A, PIP5763B) to address it.
issues.solution: Have the dealer scan the DCM for C1135 SYM92 and follow PIP5763B, which typically calls for reprogramming the Differential Control Module with updated calibration; in some cases the DCM or rear axle assembly is replaced. The N202312960 service update reflashes the DCM to correct the startup delay at no charge during the campaign window. Confirm the latest DCM software is installed before authorizing any axle hardware replacement, since the issue is usually software-related.
symptoms: Loss of torque vectoring in corners
Intermittent traction/stability warnings on cold start

citations.title: 2020-2021 Cadillac CT5-V Service Bulletin #PIP5763B: Service Rear Axle Message with DTC C1135 SYM92

communityRecommendations.content: Before any axle hardware replacement, insist the dealer verify the Differential Control Module has the latest calibration per N202312960 / PIP5763B — most cases are resolved by a reflash, not parts.
If the Service Rear Axle message comes back after a reflash, request a follow-up diagnosis: persistent C1135 SYM92 after recalibration can indicate an actual DCM hardware fault.

issues.title: 10L80 / 10L90 Harsh Shifts and Check Engine Light with DTC P2812 or P2814 (Line Pressure Solenoid)
issues.description: Owners of CT5 and CT5-V models equipped with the 10L80 (and CT5-V Blackwing's 10L90) 10-speed automatic report harsh, abrupt shifts accompanied by an illuminated check engine light. GM Preliminary Information bulletin PIP5799 documents an electrical fault in Transmission Control Solenoid Valve 7 (the line pressure solenoid) that stores DTC P2812 or P2814 in the TCM. GM separately placed certain 10L60/10L80/10L90 assemblies on PQC restriction (dealers must contact the Product Quality Center before replacing the transmission), and Recall N242480630 covers a software fix to prevent internal damage that can cause wheel lock-up.
issues.solution: Scan the TCM; if P2812 or P2814 is set, follow SI diagnostics for the line pressure solenoid circuit. PIP5799 directs that, if no other root cause is found, the valve body is replaced. Dealers are required to open a Product Quality Center (PQC) case via Dealer Case Management before replacing the transmission assembly. Also verify that GM safety Recall N242480630 (TCM monitoring software for wheel lock-up risk) has been performed; owner letters were mailed April 7, 2025.
symptoms: Rumble-strip shudder under light throttle in higher gears
Possible wheel lock-up (subject of recall N242480630)

citations.title: PIP5799 — 10L60 10L80 10L90 10L1000 Automatic Transmissions With SES Light And DTCs P2812 Or P2814 Setting
2021 10L60/10L80/10L90 10-Speed Gen II Automatic Transmission Restriction Program
Recall 257108 / N242480630 — 2019-2020 CT6, 2020-2021 CT4/CT5, 2020-2022 Camaro 10-speed transmission wheel lock-up risk

communityRecommendations.content: If you experience harsh shifts, pull codes first — a stored P2812 or P2814 points directly to the line pressure solenoid and qualifies the car for PIP5799 diagnostics under powertrain warranty.
Verify Recall N242480630 has been completed via NHTSA VIN lookup; the TCM monitoring software update is free and addresses a wheel-lock-up safety risk.

issues.title: Unwanted Automatic Emergency Braking / Reverse Automatic Braking False Activations
issues.description: Owners report the Forward Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) and Reverse Automatic Braking systems engaging without a real obstacle present — most often when reversing out of a dim garage into bright sunlight, in rain, or at low speeds with no vehicle in front. GM documented the concern broadly as 'Unwanted Integrated Brake Assist' in service bulletin N252521591 (later expanded as N252521591-02) and issued TSB 25-NA-118 providing a customer-concern verification sheet for AEB complaints. Owners on Cadillac forums confirm the CT5 and CT5-V are affected, and a class-action over similar GM AEB false activations is referenced by owners.
issues.solution: Document the conditions (lighting, weather, speed, presence/absence of obstacle) and bring the vehicle to a Cadillac dealer with TSB 25-NA-118 in hand so the tech completes the customer-concern verification sheet — this is required before GM will authorize the software remedy. The fix is typically a reflash of the radar/camera and electronic brake control modules per service update N252521591 (latest revision -02). As a workaround, the front AEB sensitivity and Reverse Automatic Braking can be turned down or off in the Driver Assistance menu while waiting for the software update.
symptoms: Car slams on brakes for no visible reason
Reverse Automatic Braking triggers when backing out of garage
False forward collision alerts in light rain or low sun
Brake pedal pulses or hard stop with no obstacle ahead

citations.title: 2020 Cadillac CT5 AWD — TSB 25-NA-118 Collision Avoidance: Automatic Emergency Braking customer-concern verification sheet (DOT Report)
GM Releases Fix For Cadillac CT5 Unwanted Brake Assist (Service Update N252521591-02)

communityRecommendations.content: Reverse Automatic Braking is most likely to false-trigger when transitioning from dim light (garage) to bright sunlight or in rain — keep a longer dwell at the threshold and watch for the rear sensor warning before applying throttle.
Bring the bulletin number (N252521591 or 25-NA-118) to your service writer. Some dealers initially deny a problem until presented with the actual GM document.

issues.title: Infotainment / Center Display Freezing, Black Screen and Stalled Software Update (stuck at 99%)
issues.description: CT5 owners report the center infotainment display freezing, becoming unresponsive to touch, or hanging during an over-the-air or dealer-pushed software update — a common symptom is a black screen with a blue progress bar stuck at 99%. The condition is documented on a 2020 CT5 case where a Cadillac-issued Technical Service Bulletin was required to be applied at the dealer to recover the module. Secondary symptoms include incorrect clock display on the instrument cluster after the screen recovers, indicating a system-wide software fault rather than a touchscreen hardware failure.
issues.solution: Try a soft reset first: press and hold the infotainment power/volume button for ~10 seconds until the Cadillac logo reappears. If the unit remains stuck (especially at 99% during an update), the fix must be performed at a Cadillac dealer per the active Cadillac TSB, which reflashes the infotainment module. Avoid interrupting any software update by shutting the car off mid-flash — that is the most common trigger for the stuck-update state. A weak 12V battery can also corrupt updates, so have battery state-of-health checked before any reflash.
symptoms: Black screen with blue progress bar stuck at 99%
Clock on cluster shows wrong time after recovery

citations.title: Cadillac CT5 Screen Frozen at 99 Percent How to Reset? (2020 CT5, JustAnswer expert references active Cadillac TSB)

communityRecommendations.content: If the screen is mid-update, do NOT shut the engine off — let the update complete (5-15 minutes). Interrupting the flash is the #1 cause of the stuck-at-99% state.
Have battery state-of-health tested before any dealer-pushed reflash; a weak 12V battery can corrupt the update and create exactly the freeze symptom the bulletin addresses.
